title: Courier Down
summary: Rill Davenant's beacon went dark between the survey camp and the turbine row — mid-run, no storm close enough to blame, no distress call proud enough to be hers. Her transponder's fragments are pinging along the row like teeth after a bar fight. Recover them, follow what's left of the signal up the ridge, and bring Ketch proof of something. Any something.

objectives.label: Start from Rill's last logged waypoint at the survey camp
Recover 4 transponder fragments along the turbine row
Follow the last broken signal up to the ridge crest
Bring the fragments home to the garage

offer.text: Board's yours, kid. Missing courier. North loop, survey camp to the turbines. Pieces of her transponder are pinging along the row.
Ketch. That's the shortest briefing you've ever given. You okay?

accept.text: Four pips on the row. Find them all. Don't improvise, don't hero, don't stop to read the weather. Flat salt.

Varga — off the record, which is a phrase the Guild charges for. Davenant's manifest was *clean*. No cargo worth robbing, no route worth racing. Whatever happened to her didn't want her freight. It wanted her route.
Courier. Reverb. The desert's been saying the tall one's name for two days, wrong, the way it does. Except today it's saying it past tense. Hurry up.

complete.text: Ketch. Four fragments, all from the port pannier. The beacon didn't die — it was *switched off*, gentle as a lamp. And the crest… I found her jacket. Tied to a tower leg like a flag. Knot-side facing the hollow.
Thirty years I told you kids the storms were the worst thing out there. Jacket's on my bench. Radio's off. Door's open. Come home whenever, kid. I'll be up.
Station. My radio carried something at dusk that was not a storm. It was counting couriers the way the Guild counts salt. It had a number for Davenant, station. It has a number for you.
